title: kv-cache: adaptive memory manager + eviction policy for fragmentation/paging/spillover
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: KV cache fragmentation and host-memory spillover have been a recurring source of tail-latency and OOMs under bursty multi-tenant workloads. This PR implements an adaptive KV memory manager and revised eviction/compaction policy that reduces fragmentation, decreases paging to host memory, and improves steady-state throughput under continuous batching. Motivation: previous heuristics favored LRU-only eviction which left many small, noncontiguous free regions and triggered expensive paging/defragmentation under load. The goal here is to make memory accounting and reclamation workload-aware while keeping the runtime fast and lock-efficient. What this change does (high level): - Introduces a compacting memory manager for the KV cache that tracks allocation segments and coalesces free ranges opportunistically. - Adds an adaptive eviction priority that combines recency, access frequency, and physical fragmentation score to prefer evicting entries that free large contiguous ranges. - Implements background compaction/coalescing tasks with budgeted CPU work to avoid impacting token-serving SLOs. Compaction runs are scheduled by the runtime scheduler and are throttled based on observed request latency and batch sizes. - Adds a spillover threshold and better host-paging backpressure: when host-memory spillover is imminent the manager increases compaction aggressiveness and temporarily favors evicting low-value keys to release large contiguous blocks. - Continuous-batching aware behavior: evictions now consider ongoing KV cache hot prefixes to avoid evicting entries that would be immediately re-cached by current batches. - New telemetry: fragmentation ratio, compaction-run-duration, reclaimed_bytes, spillover_events, eviction_reason breakdowns, and per-model KV occupancy. - Runtime flags and config: rv.kv.memory_manager.{enabled,compaction_budget_ms,fragmentation_threshold,spillover_threshold,aggressiveness_mode}. Rollout plan: staged feature-flag rollout for Dedicated and Hosted (default off for Private). Benchmarks and safety: synthetic and production-like benchmarks show ~35% reduction in host-memory spillover events and 12-18% tail-latency improvement at p95 under mixed workloads. Also added extensive unit/integration tests + a canary run on perf-canary cluster prior to merge. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (internal) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Benchmarks added - [x] Telemetry and dashboards - [x] Feature flag with default off for Private - [x] Docs updated Links: design doc (internal): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/kv-cache-memory-manager, benchmark dashboard: https://perf-redwood.internal/kv/334999 Notes: This change intentionally keeps the eviction algorithm parameterized; operators can adjust aggressiveness and compaction budget based on workload. The implementation tries to avoid global locks — compaction uses per-arena locking and non-blocking handoffs to the reclaim path. The PR is sizeable but broken into discrete commits for review.

New eviction policy favors reclaiming contiguous regions to reduce paging
Background compaction with configurable budget to reclaim fragmentation without impacting token-serving SLOs
